title: Equinox Systems — Integration & Deployment Discovery
summary: Discovery call to evaluate Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private for Equinox's search+RAG product. Primary concerns: latency/cost tradeoffs, integration with LangChain/LlamaIndex, running behind an internal gateway/proxy, VPC and KMS for private deployments, and observability hooks for token-level cost and traceability. Agreed to run a small perf benchmark and exchange security docs; follow-up pilot proposed.
topics: gateway/proxy patterns and sidecar vs centralized gateway
observability hooks: traces, logs, token-level cost
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/KMS) security requirements
action_items: Maya Chen: Share Redwood SOC2 + Security whitepaper (2026-10-14)
Ravi Patel: Provide sample LangChain adapter snippet and LlamaIndex example (2026-10-15)
Priya Sharma (Equinox): Send sample request distribution and average seq lengths (2026-10-16)
Noah Ruiz: Draft pilot runbook and perf test plan (2026-10-19)
next_steps: Redwood to send security docs and pricing tiers for Hosted/Dedicated/Private
Customer to provide token/traffic profile spreadsheet
Schedule 60-min technical pilot kickoff (proposed week of 2026-10-26)
Run 3-day perf benchmark comparing Hosted small model vs Dedicated quantized instance
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-10-12 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Noah Ruiz (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Equinox Head of ML), Priya Sharma (Platform), Derek Wu (Security), Ana Torres (SRE)

Auto Summary: Evaluating integration surface for Equinox's RAG/search product. Questions around SDKs, LangChain/LlamaIndex adapters, running behind their gateway, rate limits and quotas, and observability. Security and VPC/KMS requirements discussed. Concrete next steps and pilot agreed.

[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro on our side, I'm Maya AE, with Ravi and Noah from our solutions engineering team. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:12] Liam O'Connor: Good, thanks. Appreciate you fitting this in. We wanted to run through integration options and get a sense of where Redwood fits into our infra — particularly whether we go hosted, dedicated reserved capacity, or private VPC.
[00:00:25] Maya Chen: Totally. rough agenda: integration surface area with SDKs and the common libraries you might use — LangChain, LlamaIndex — then gateway/proxy patterns you all mentioned, rate limiting/quotas, and observability hooks. Then security and pilot next steps. Does that sound right?
[00:00:40] Priya Sharma: Yup. We'll probably jump in on the infra questions.
[00:00:44] Ravi Patel: Quick note, I might dive into some perf and batching details later, and Noah will cover SDK snippets and adapter code.
[00:00:50] Ana Torres: From SRE's pov we'll want to understand network egress, VPC peering, and what telemetry we can ingest into our existing Prometheus/Grafana stacks.

[00:01:05] Liam O'Connor: For context, our product handles user search with a RAG layer. Typical request: user query + 2-3 docs, average prompt length is ~350 tokens, replies are ~250 tokens. Peak QPS during business hours is about 45 QPS, with bursts to 120 QPS. Latency SLO is sub-300ms for the first token ideally, 95th pct under 800ms for full response. Cost is material — we need to evaluate cost per 1k tokens as well as unit economics for dedicated.
[00:01:35] Ravi Patel: Good, that's super helpful. A few immediate notes: 350/250 seqs are friendly to our runtime. For that traffic profile, Dedicated usually gives best predictability, Hosted can be cheaper to start but you see more variance on latency during noisy neighbors, and Private/VPC gives you the control for compliance.

[00:01:55] Derek Wu: On security — we need data in transit encrypted, customer-managed KMS for keys, audit logs retention for 12 months, and SSO/SAML integration. We're also under SOC2.
[00:02:08] Maya Chen: That's standard ask. We offer KMS integrations, SOC2 docs, and audit log exports. I'll share our security pack after this call.

[00:02:18] [00:02:20] Noah Ruiz: Jumping into SDKs — Redwood has first-party SDKs in Python, JS, and go. For LangChain/LlamaIndex, we have adapters and example notebooks. In python you'd use redwood.Client(...) or the higher-level LLM wrapper. There's also streaming websockets support if you need token-level streaming.
[00:02:44] Priya Sharma: Do you have a drop-in LangChain LLM wrapper? We already use LangChain in prod.
[00:02:50] Noah Ruiz: Yes, we provide a connector: from redwood import RedwoodLLM then you can pass it to LangChain's chains. The adapter handles retries and token accounting. For LlamaIndex we have a similar integration but sometimes naming in the docs is a bit off — we saw issues with model names autofilling. We'll send sample snippets.
[00:03:10] Liam O'Connor: And for LlamaIndex are there any limitations around the KV cache or persistent indices?
[00:03:16] Ravi Patel: LlamaIndex's storage layer is independent. Redwood manages the model KV cache — the server-side cache for key-value attention state — which doesn't affect your index store. If you're doing a vector DB and then passing context, that's standard. We also offer prefix caching for common query templates to reduce cost.

[00:03:35] [00:03:40] Priya Sharma: About gateway/proxy — we run a centralized API gateway and prefer not to change client code. Can Redwood operate behind a proxy or as a sidecar?
[00:03:50] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Two common patterns: 1) Centralized gateway where your API calls outbound to Redwood hosted endpoints (or Dedicated endpoints) — you control auth and do tokenization/ratelimiting at the gateway. 2) Sidecar or private connector where an internal sidecar handles auth + request routing to Redwood Private deployment within your VPC. Sidecar reduces cross-region egress but adds ops overhead.
[00:04:15] Ana Torres: If we pick Private, do you deploy into our VPC or do we connect back to Redwood control plane?
[00:04:22] Ravi Patel: We offer a private control plane with a customer-managed data plane option. For fully air-gapped or on-prem we run a local package. For VPC, we deploy shaded workers in your VPC that talk to a control plane via an encrypted channel; keys can be managed by your KMS.

[00:04:40] Derek Wu: What about firewall rules and least privilege? We can't allow broad egress to the internet.
[00:04:46] Noah Ruiz: Our VPC option supports sg/acl whitelisting of control plane IPs, and for Dedicated we can provide static egress IPs for allowlisting. For Hosted, it's trickier because it's multi-tenant.

[00:04:58] [00:05:05] Liam O'Connor: Rate limits and quotas — we want to enforce per-team quotas and burst credits. Can Redwood enforce per-api-key quotas at the edge so we don't need to build our own quota layer?
[00:05:15] Ravi Patel: We have per-token quotas and per-key rate limits that can be applied at the tenant or route level. For Dedicated, you get more granular policies and can configure burst behaviors. Hosted supports simple per-key caps plus enterprise-level configurable policies. You can also push down your own gateway's quota to avoid double counting.

[00:05:35] Priya Sharma: How are throttles surfaced? HTTP 429 with a retry-after? Any webhook for quota alerts?
[00:05:41] Noah Ruiz: Yes 429 + Retry-After for runtime throttles. We also provide webhooks and an events API for quota alerts and billing threshold notifications that you can hook into your ops channels.

[00:05:55] [00:06:05] Ana Torres: Observability — we need traces and token-level cost breakdown; ability to add trace ids across request flow into our logging.
[00:06:13] Ravi Patel: Observability is something our Console exposes: per-route latency breakdown, token cost attribution, and spans for request lifecycle. We export traces via OpenTelemetry and logs via a push-to-s3 or syslog. For token-level cost you'd get token counts and the model variant used; you can correlate that with your request_id.
[00:06:33] Liam O'Connor: Are these hooks available in Private deployments as well?
[00:06:37] Maya Chen: Yes, the same observability primitives are available. For Private you control where the telemetry goes — we can push traces into your OTEL collector.

[00:06:50] [00:07:00] Priya Sharma: On model variants — can we pin to a quantized model for cost predictability and fall back to a higher-quality variant on error?
[00:07:08] Ravi Patel: Yes. We have model pinning and fallback policies. You can route by policy (latency vs cost) and fallback to compatible variants. In Dedicated setups you can also pin model versions to specific GPU pools.

[00:07:22] Derek Wu: For compliance, we also need to ensure data isn't used for model training. Is that an opt-in or opt-out?
[00:07:29] Maya Chen: For enterprise contracts we provide a non-training clause and data retention controls. We'll include the legal language in the security pack.

[00:07:36] [00:07:45] Liam O'Connor: For the pilot we want to validate 95th pct latency under 800ms at 50qps sustained and cost baseline. What would you recommend as a pilot configuration?
[00:07:55] Ravi Patel: I'd suggest a short Dedicated pilot: reserved capacity sized to your 50qps target using a quantized model, with a fallback to Hosted or a bigger Dedicated pool for bursting. That lets you validate SLOs and cost. Alternatively, we can start with Hosted for quick evaluation then migrate to Dedicated. There's a tradeoff in setup time vs fidelity.

[00:08:17] Priya Sharma: How long to get Dedicated reserved pools live?
[00:08:21] Noah Ruiz: For standard regions, provisioning can be 2–5 business days after contract and capacity sizing. Private VPC deploys take longer — typically 2–3 weeks for initial setup and certs.

[00:08:33] [00:08:45] Maya Chen: Quick heads-up on pricing: hosted per-token pricing, dedicated is committed monthly with better unit economics, and private has platform fees plus infra. I'll share a pricing sheet with tiered examples.

[00:08:55] Derek Wu: If we do Private, is there a managed option where Redwood handles upgrades?
[00:09:00] Ravi Patel: Yes, we offer a managed private deployment where Redwood handles runtime upgrades and security patches; you still keep control of network and keys. On-prem fully self-managed is also available.

[00:09:10] [00:09:20] Liam O'Connor: About SDK reliability — do your SDKs handle streaming reconnects and partial responses? We can't have duplicate tokens causing billing anomalies.
[00:09:30] Noah Ruiz: The SDK has idempotency keys and de-duplication for streaming reconnects, and token accounting is conservative: we track confirmed tokens. There are edge cases but we log those and surface them in the Console.

[00:09:48] Priya Sharma: Integration path — if we wanted to wire up LangChain quickly, what's the minimal code?
[00:09:55] Noah Ruiz: We'll send a 6-line snippet but roughly: install redwood client, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, then pass RedwoodLLM into LangChain. We'll attach retry strategy and a streaming callback to capture partials. I'll paste the snippet in the follow-up.

[00:10:10] [00:10:20] Maya Chen: Any other concerns on the security side?
[00:10:23] Derek Wu: Encryption at rest for logs, KMS integration, and SIEM forwarding. Also need proof of pen test and vuln scan cadence.
[00:10:30] Maya Chen: We'll include SOC2 report, pen test summary, and our vulnerability disclosure cadence in the pack.

[00:10:40] [00:10:58] Liam O'Connor: A random thought — for our latency-critical flows we sometimes prewarm cache with frequent queries. Do you support prefix caching or prewarmed sessions?
[00:11:05] Ravi Patel: Yes, prefix/KV caching and warmup requests are supported. We also have a continuous batching engine that groups requests where possible without adding tail latency. There's knobs to tweak batching windows per-route.

[00:11:25] Priya Sharma: On billing we need token-level granularity to reconcile costs to product lines. Does the Console give per-route cost allocation?
[00:11:33] Noah Ruiz: Yes, per-route token and cost breakdown. You can map keys to cost centers and export daily CSVs or push to S3.

[00:11:45] [00:12:00] Maya Chen: Let me propose a pilot scope: 3-day Dedicated pilot sized for 50qps with quantized model, run your synthetic traffic (Priya will share distribution), collect 95th pct latency metrics and cost. We'll provide access to the Console and the LangChain/LlamaIndex snippets. Anything to add?
[00:12:18] Priya Sharma: Also need to validate trace export to OTEL collector and quota webhook to our ops channel.
[00:12:24] Ana Torres: And we'd like static egress IPs for allowlisting during the pilot.

[00:12:30] Ravi Patel: We can supply static IPs for Dedicated and VPC config. We'll include OTEL exporter config in the runbook.

[00:12:40] [00:12:50] Liam O'Connor: Great. On timelines, if we kick off the pilot the week of Oct 26, when would we expect results?
[00:12:57] Maya Chen: Pilot results in 1 week for initial perf numbers; full analysis in 2 weeks including cost modeling. So you'd see numbers by mid-November if we start Oct 26.

[00:13:10] Priya Sharma: Any blockers from Redwood side to get SOC docs and SDK samples?
[00:13:14] Maya Chen: None. I'll put them in an email and upload to the shared folder.

[00:13:20] [00:13:30] Noah Ruiz: Quick technical caveat — if you use LlamaIndex with very long contexts (2k+ tokens), cost and latency dynamics change, and we'll suggest different kernel/path optimizations. For your 350/250 averages we're in good shape.

[00:13:47] Derek Wu: For contracts we need a data processing addendum and a non-training clause, plus a 12-month log retention SLA.
[00:13:55] Maya Chen: Noted. We'll route legal to legal and include standard DPAs and addenda.

[00:14:05] [00:14:20] Liam O'Connor: Anything else? I just want to make sure we don't miss the quota/alerting integration piece.
[00:14:27] Ravi Patel: We will provide webhooks, events API, and can integrate with Slack/pager duty for alerts. Also recommend client-side rate limiting to smooth bursts.

[00:14:40] Priya Sharma: We may run a POC where some teams use Hosted and others use Dedicated. Is that supported?
[00:14:48] Maya Chen: Yes, customers often run a hybrid: dev on Hosted, production on Dedicated/Private. Our routing policies can route by key or region so it's straightforward.

[00:15:00] [00:15:10] Ana Torres: Operational question — how do we rotate keys with minimal downtime?
[00:15:15] Noah Ruiz: We support rolling API key rotation and ephemeral tokens. For session migration there's an overlap window; we document the exact sequence in the runbook.

[00:15:28] Maya Chen: Okay, let's recap and confirm owners. Action items: I'll send security pack and pricing; Ravi and Noah will send SDK snippets and runbook; Priya sends traffic profile; Noah drafts pilot runbook.

[00:15:42] [00:15:55] Liam O'Connor: Sounds good. Appreciate the detail. We'll review the security docs and pricing and come back with any gating items.

[00:16:05] Maya Chen: Great — thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the materials by Thursday.
[00:16:12] Priya Sharma: Thank you.
[00:16:15] Derek Wu: Thanks all.

[00:16:20] End of recording. Note: transcription has occasional mis-hearings of product names and minor punctuation errors.
